chapter: Alcohol, Paris and the hit record
title: Living with Uncle Louie in Paris without working
summary: He did not work in Paris, living in his uncle's apartment near the Eiffel Tower; his uncle worked for the American government.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Were you still not feeling well when you were in Europe, when you first went -- you're in Paris with your Uncle Louie and you're there for about three years.
Are you working as a musician across that time?

No, no. I didn't work at all. I didn't have to because my uncle, they had a large one- floor apartment. My uncle and my Aunt Flowers [phonetic sp.], and had a maid. I mean, it had maid quarters upstairs. I mean, it was really. And we were right there. We'd open up the -- the ­ - the blinds -- not the blinds, but the shutters, and Eiffel Tower would be standing right there. I mean, we were right there. We were in hell of an [indiscernible], I mean, a wonderful
And what did your uncle do?
He -- he worked for the government, the American government. Yeah, he -- he -- he got housing for the -- the military. And he worked. He was a civil servant. He did that, yeah.
And you learned to speak French while you were there?

No. I didn't learn there then. I learned afterwards because everybody I knew, they were like, they spoke English and they were -- there were like American, they hung together. You know. Birds of a feather. You know. Always stick together as they say. I thought -- when I came back, I felt so ashamed. I said, "Damn! Let me try to learn a few words here." You know. Yeah.
